title: Stop Arguing About Who's Right
coreMove: Hold your story as one coherent version and ask what the other person sees that your position cannot see.
sourcePressure: The chapter replaces message delivery with the learning stance and stresses that performed openness is not the same as genuine curiosity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Being nicer while still trying to deliver a verdict.

sourceAnchors.name: message delivery stance and learning stance
sourceAnchors.detail: The source contrasts delivering your version as truth with entering to learn what each person sees and what may be missing.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A learning stance begins when your own story stops acting like the room's legal record.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.

hook: Do not open ch02 with a generic dread-before-meeting frame
Do not begin with a definition of the chapter term
Do not use a negotiation-table abstraction as the first image
counterintuition: Avoid the shell 'you think X, but actually Y'
Avoid claiming the idea is simply counterintuitive
Avoid treating compassion as the surprising twist
tryThisNow: No 'pause and reflect on your communication style' action
examples: Avoid repeated coffee-table, classroom, narrow-kitchen, bus-depot, marker, mug, or radiator shells
Avoid six workplace meetings with changed names
Avoid making every case a manager feedback scene

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: use these six opening devices in order: question-as-hook; sensory detail first; dialogue first line; timestamp+name+action; environmental detail before any human; retrospective first line
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: co-founders stuck in competing true stories
exampleSpecs.stakes: four weeks of delay is threatening a customer pilot
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire closes the feature spreadsheet and asks Jonas what user risk he sees that her dashboard does not show
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laptop trackpad worn shiny beside a roadmap spreadsheet

exampleSpecs.audience: curators revising public interpretation under deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: the opening preview is in nine days and each curator thinks the other is distorting the exhibit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one curator reads the other's annotated label as a complete story rather than a mistake to correct
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glass case reflecting two different label drafts

exampleSpecs.domain: couple dividing night-shift care for a newborn
exampleSpecs.audience: partners exhausted by a fairness argument
exampleSpecs.stakes: sleep deprivation is turning every request into evidence of selfishness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one partner asks what the night feels like from the other side before reopening the tally
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I am not asking for a scorecard," one partner says

exampleSpecs.audience: board members with values conflict masquerading as facts
exampleSpecs.stakes: a grant vote could cut either housing support or legal aid
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew writes the sentence he wants to deliver, then crosses it out and writes one question he does not know the answer to
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grant rubric printed on heavy cream paper

exampleSpecs.stakes: a model review has become a fight about taste instead of constraints
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kiran asks which constraint Margaux is optimizing for before defending his facade choice
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cardboard model casting a crooked shadow

exampleSpecs.domain: parents choosing a high school program
exampleSpecs.audience: family members reading the same brochure differently
exampleSpecs.stakes: the child is beginning to treat the parents' argument as a verdict on her future
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Margaux maps each parent's fear beside each claimed fact before the family meeting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: school brochures spread across a dining table

skillTargets: identify when a scenario needs hold your story as one coherent version and ask what the other person sees that your position cannot see.
distinguish message delivery stance from the adjacent generic misread
choose the visible action that demonstrates the chapter move rather than merely naming it
explain why the wrong option would recreate being nicer while still trying to deliver a verdict.

tryThisNowSpec: Rewrite the sentence you most want to deliver as one question whose answer could genuinely alter your view.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
